facts.summary: AWS VPC three-tier application architecture with an ALB, Application Service, and RDS Database segmented across subnets.
relationships: Internet forwards traffic to ALB over HTTPS
ALB forwards traffic to Application Service over HTTP
Application Service queries RDS Database over SQL
Security-group rules restrict traffic at each hop

facts.summary: A three-tier AWS VPC architecture directing traffic from the Internet to an ALB, then to an Application Service, and finally to an RDS Database.
relationships: Internet routes HTTPS to Application Load Balancer
Application Load Balancer routes HTTP to Application Service
Application Service communicates SQL to RDS Database
ALB, App Service, and RDS reside within VPC 10.0.0.0/16

facts.summary: A three-tier AWS VPC architecture directing traffic from the Internet through an ALB and Application Service to an RDS Database restricted by security groups.
relationships: Internet sends HTTPS to Application Load Balancer
Application Load Balancer sends HTTP to Application Service
Application Service sends SQL to RDS Database
ALB, Application Service, and RDS are hosted in VPC

facts.summary: Architecture showing CloudFront as the sole public entry directing traffic to a private ALB origin serving an EKS backend inside a VPC.
relationships: Users send HTTPS requests to CloudFront
CloudFront forwards requests to Private ALB as origin
Private ALB forwards HTTP requests to EKS Service
Private ALB and EKS Service reside inside the VPC

facts.summary: Architecture diagram depicting private OpenSearch Serverless vector search access via a VPC Endpoint with reader and ingester separation.
relationships: Backend Reader sends read requests to VPC Endpoint
OIDC Corpus Ingester sends write requests to VPC Endpoint
VPC Endpoint routes private traffic to OpenSearch Serverless

facts.summary: Object content and relational metadata split architecture where uploads are decoupled into S3 byte storage and MariaDB metadata.
relationships: User Upload sends upload to Spring Boot API
Spring Boot API writes metadata to MariaDB
Spring Boot API writes bytes to S3 Bucket
